hub.description: Decks and fences for Goodlettsville, TN, from worn decks on older ranch lots to newer builds, plus how permits work on each side of the county line.
hub.intro: Goodlettsville sits across the line between Davidson and Sumner counties, and its houses cover a wide range. Many streets are lined with older ranch homes on established lots, often with a wood deck out back that is past its best years. Close by, newer builds sit on yards the builder graded and seeded, with nothing behind the house yet. Around Rivergate, where some homes sit near shopping and busy roads, a solid fence that blocks the view is often high on the list. Old house or new, most projects come down to a deck that is safe to stand on or a fence that gives the yard some privacy. Below is what shapes both jobs in Goodlettsville. For more detail, see our [Goodlettsville deck builder page](/deck-builder-goodlettsville-tn/) and the page on [fence installation in Goodlettsville](/fence-company-goodlettsville-tn/).

sections.heading: Older ranch homes and the decks behind them
paragraphs: Plenty of Goodlettsville homes are single story ranch houses that have stood for decades. Many of them picked up a wood deck somewhere along the way, and a lot of those decks are now wearing out. The first signs are usually a railing that gives when you lean on it and boards that feel soft near the door. The bigger worries are harder to see: rot where the deck meets the house and posts that have sat in damp ground for years. Deck rules have also tightened over time, especially around how a deck is fastened to the house. An old deck that looked fine when it went up may not match what an inspector expects today.

The back door on many Goodlettsville ranch houses is only a few steps above the yard, so a replacement deck tends to be low and fairly simple to frame. That can leave more room in the budget for better boards or a wider set of stairs. It also means the space under the deck is tight, which affects airflow and how long the framing lasts.

sections.heading: Newer builds and yards that start from scratch
paragraphs: Goodlettsville also has newer houses mixed in among the older ones, and the yards behind them are a different job. A builder shaped that ground to move rainwater away from the foundation, often toward a low swale near a property line. The soil against the house is fill that went back in after the foundation was poured, and it is looser than the ground farther out. Deck footings have to go through that fill to firm soil. A fence line has to cross the swale without blocking it. Many of these newer Goodlettsville neighborhoods also have an HOA with its own review, so plan for that approval before you plan a start date.

sections.heading: What is under a Goodlettsville yard
paragraphs: Like much of Middle Tennessee, Goodlettsville has limestone below the soil, and in some yards it sits close to the surface. The soil above it is often heavy clay that stays wet after a hard rain and shrinks as it dries in late summer. Neither one rules out a deck or a fence. Rock can slow down digging, though, and nobody can say how much is down there until the auger finds it. The shape of the land matters as well. Some Goodlettsville yards are fairly flat, while others fall away toward a creek or a low corner of the lot. A sloped yard changes how tall a deck gets on the low side and how a fence follows the ground.

sections.heading: Which codes office covers your lot
paragraphs: Because the county line runs through Goodlettsville, a Goodlettsville mailing address does not tell you who handles permits. The house could be inside Goodlettsville city limits. It could also fall under a different office, such as Metro Nashville on the Davidson side, or the county or a neighboring city on the Sumner side. Each office has its own process for decks, and fence rules can differ from one to the next. Your property tax records usually show which one applies. Once you know, call that codes office and ask what your project needs before any work is scheduled. Our guide on [deck permits in Tennessee](/guides/deck-permits-tennessee/) covers the general steps. HOA approval, if you have one, is a separate step on top of the permit.

sections.heading: Big trees and creek lots
paragraphs: Established lots in Goodlettsville often come with large shade trees. Shade feels good in July, but a deck under a heavy canopy stays damp longer and tends to grow mildew. That can steer you toward one kind of board over another. Roots also matter. A fence line or a row of deck footings that runs past a big trunk needs some planning so the digging does not damage the tree.

Some Goodlettsville homes sit near Mansker Creek or one of the smaller streams in the area. Low ground near a creek can stay soggy for days after rain, and parts of some lots fall inside a mapped flood zone. Building rules are stricter in a flood zone, so if your yard runs down toward the water, ask the codes office about it early. It is much easier to plan around than to fix after the posts are in.

faqs.q: How do I find out if my house is inside Goodlettsville city limits?
faqs.a: Start with your property tax bill or the county property records, which usually show whether a city is part of the taxing district. If the City of Goodlettsville is listed, the city codes office is your first call. If it is not, you are likely under Metro Nashville, Sumner County, or another nearby city, depending on which side of the line you are on. When in doubt, call the city with your address and ask.

faqs.q: Can a new deck go in the same spot as my old one?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Keeping the same footprint is often the simplest choice, since the door and the path to the yard already work. What rarely carries over is the structure. Old footings may be too small or too shallow for current rules, and the spot where the old deck met the house needs a close look for rot once the boards come off. In many cases that means new footings and a new frame, even if the shape stays the same.

faqs.q: Does my HOA need to approve a deck or fence in a newer Goodlettsville neighborhood?
faqs.a: If your subdivision has an HOA, the answer is usually yes. Most committees want a simple drawing that shows where the project goes and what it will look like. Fences tend to get the closest look because neighbors see them from the street. Send the request before you book a crew, and keep a copy of the approval. Our guide on [getting HOA approval](/guides/hoa-approval-deck-fence/) walks through what to include.

deck.description: Deck builder in Goodlettsville, TN: replacing worn decks on older ranch homes, first decks on newer builds, and what rock and slope mean for footings.
deck.intro: Many decks in Goodlettsville are old enough to need replacing. A common picture is a ranch house that has stood for decades, with a wood deck added later that now has soft boards by the door and loose railing posts. Newer houses around town have the opposite problem. The back door opens onto a short drop and maybe a few pavers, with no deck at all. Either way, you need a deck builder who sets the frame on solid footings and ties it to the house correctly. Here is what that looks like on a Goodlettsville lot.

sections.heading: Replacing an older deck in Goodlettsville
paragraphs: Surface wear is easy to spot. Gray, splintered boards and flaking stain look bad, but they do not mean the deck is unsafe. The trouble that matters sits lower. Push a screwdriver into the posts right at the ground and into the joists near the house. If it sinks in, the wood is rotting. The ledger, which is the board fastened to the house that carries one side of the deck, deserves a close look for dark streaks or soft spots. Stairs that flex are another warning. On many older decks the ledger was nailed on without flashing, which lets water sit behind it for years.

If the framing is sound, new boards and railings on the old frame can make sense. On many Goodlettsville decks this age, though, the frame and footings are the real problem, and a full replacement is the safer call. Our guide on [signs your deck is done](/guides/signs-you-need-a-new-deck/) goes through the checks in more detail. When you collect bids, ask each deck builder whether tearing out the old deck and hauling it off are included, since that part of the work is easy to leave out of a price.

sections.heading: Low decks on ranch houses
paragraphs: Many ranch homes in Goodlettsville sit only a few steps above the yard, so the deck behind them is usually low. Low decks are simpler to frame, and whether they need a railing depends on the height and local rules. The catch is what happens underneath. When the joists sit close to the dirt, air barely moves under there and the wood stays damp. Framing that close to the ground should be lumber rated for ground contact. The soil below should also slope away from the house so water does not pond under the boards.

Some older ranch houses in Goodlettsville also have a small concrete patio or stoop at the back door. It is tempting to set deck posts right on that slab, but a patio slab was rarely poured to carry that kind of load. The usual answer is to frame around it or take it out and put proper footings in the ground. On lots that fall away from the back of the house, a ranch can have a walkout basement below. Then the deck sits a full story up, which calls for heavier posts and a real staircase.

sections.heading: Footings in Goodlettsville rock and clay
paragraphs: Every deck post sits on a footing, and the footing has to reach below the depth where the ground freezes in winter. In Goodlettsville that often means digging through clay and, in some yards, running into limestone before the hole is deep enough. When that happens, the fix might be drilling into the rock or shifting the footing a little and adjusting the frame to match. What works depends on how much rock there is and what the inspector accepts. Clay brings its own issue. It swells when wet and shrinks when dry, so footings need to bear on firm, undisturbed soil rather than loose fill. Ask how a bid handles rock before you sign, because it is one of the few costs nobody can see in advance.

sections.heading: Decks for newer Goodlettsville houses
paragraphs: On a newer Goodlettsville build, the house is sound but the yard has not settled in. The ground right against the foundation is backfill, so footings near the house have to go past it to reach firm soil. The ledger connection needs flashing tied into the house wrap so water sheds away from the rim, which often means pulling back some siding and putting it back cleanly. If your neighborhood has an HOA, the architectural committee will likely want a simple drawing and a note on the board color. Get that approval in writing before work is scheduled.

sections.heading: Permits when the county line runs through town
paragraphs: A deck that is attached to the house or raised off the ground usually needs a permit. Here the first job is figuring out whose permit it is. Inside city limits, that is the City of Goodlettsville codes office. Outside those limits, a house with a Goodlettsville address might fall under Metro Nashville, or under the county or a neighboring city on the Sumner side. Each office has its own forms and inspection steps. A permitted deck also protects you later, since buyers and their inspectors often ask about decks when a house goes on the market. Our [Tennessee deck permit guide](/guides/deck-permits-tennessee/) covers the general process, but confirm the details with the office that handles your address.

sections.heading: Choosing boards for shaded and sunny yards
paragraphs: Pressure treated pine is one of the most common deck boards around Middle Tennessee. It costs less up front and takes stain well, but it needs cleaning and sealing every so often to keep from cracking and turning gray. Composite boards cost more at the start and need less upkeep, though they can get hot underfoot in full afternoon sun. On an established Goodlettsville lot with big trees overhead, shade is the bigger concern. Wood under heavy shade stays damp and can grow mildew, and composite can too, so plan on a regular wash either way. Our comparison of [wood and composite decking](/guides/wood-vs-composite-decking/) goes deeper.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace my deck in Goodlettsville?
faqs.a: In most cases, yes. Replacing a deck usually means new footings and a new frame, and codes offices tend to treat that as new construction rather than a repair. Which office you apply to depends on where your lot falls relative to city limits and the county line. Call the right one with your address and a rough sketch of the deck, and ask what they need to see before work starts.

faqs.q: Can I keep my old deck frame and just replace the boards?
faqs.a: Sometimes. If the joists and posts are solid and the ledger is properly fastened and flashed, new boards and railings on the old frame can be a fair choice. Many older decks in Goodlettsville fail that test, though. Putting new boards on a frame with only a few years left means paying for boards twice. Have the frame checked from below, or with a few boards pulled, before you decide.

faqs.q: What happens to the old deck when it comes down?
faqs.a: The old boards and framing have to go somewhere, and so do the concrete footings. Some builders include tear out and hauling in the price, and some list it separately or leave it to you. Old pressure treated lumber should not be burned, so it usually goes to a landfill that accepts it. Ask every bidder to spell out removal in writing, including whether old footings get pulled or cut down below the soil.

faqs.q: My Goodlettsville yard slopes away from the house. What changes?
faqs.a: It comes up on plenty of Goodlettsville lots, whether you live near Rivergate or off Long Hollow Pike. The deck gets taller on the low side, which means longer posts and more bracing. If the drop is steep, stairs take up more room than people expect, so think about where they will land in the yard. A sloped lot can also be a chance to add a landing partway down instead of one long run of steps. Footings on a slope need to sit in firm ground, not in soil that could wash out.

faqs.q: What should a written deck bid include?
faqs.a: A good bid names the deck size and the materials for the boards and railings. It should explain how the frame attaches to the house and who pulls the permit. Look for a line about rock, since some Goodlettsville yards hit limestone when the footings are dug. If one deck builder comes in far below the rest, check what the bid leaves out before you assume it is the better deal.

fence.description: Fence installation in Goodlettsville, TN: privacy fences for older lots, busy roads near Rivergate, and newer HOA yards, and why property lines come first.
fence.intro: Fence projects in Goodlettsville tend to start from one of a few places. On older lots there is usually a fence already standing, either tired wood or chain link that has rusted and sagged. Homeowners closer to Rivergate, where busy roads and shopping are not far away, often want a solid fence to block the view. In newer subdivisions the yard may have no fence at all, just a dog who needs somewhere to run. Each case calls for different questions before fence installation starts, and this page goes through them for a Goodlettsville yard.

sections.heading: Old fences on established Goodlettsville lots
paragraphs: Many older lots in Goodlettsville already have some kind of fence, and taking it out is the first part of the job. Chain link comes down fairly easily, but the posts are often set in concrete that has to be dug or broken out. Old wood fences often leave rotted post stubs in the ground, sometimes right where the new posts want to go. Neighbors matter here too. If the fence along the back was put up by the people next door, it may be theirs, and it may not sit on the property line at all.

Before you tear anything down, talk with the neighbor who shares the line. In some cases the old fence belongs to them and stays, and the new one goes just inside it. In others, both of you want the same privacy fence and can agree on the plan together. Either way, it saves an awkward conversation after work begins. Ask each fence company that bids whether removing and hauling off the old fence is part of the price, because it is easy to leave out.

sections.heading: Property lines come first
paragraphs: On a Goodlettsville lot that was laid out long ago, the corner pins may be buried or missing entirely. An old fence line or a row of shrubs is not proof of where the line runs. If you are not sure where your corners are, a survey is worth paying for before fence installation, and it usually costs less than moving a finished fence. Tennessee 811 also needs a call before anyone digs, so buried utility lines get marked. Newer subdivisions usually have a recorded plat to check against, but on older lots the paperwork can be thin. Our guide to [fences and property lines](/guides/fence-property-line-tennessee/) explains the rest.

sections.heading: Privacy fences near Rivergate and busy roads
paragraphs: Some homes near the Rivergate area sit closer to shopping and heavier traffic than much of Goodlettsville, and a solid privacy fence is often the goal. Board on board is a good fit because the boards overlap. As the wood shrinks in dry weather, the gaps stay covered instead of opening up. Shadowbox looks about the same from both sides, which neighbors tend to appreciate, though it lets a little more view through at an angle. Our rundown of [privacy fence options](/guides/privacy-fence-options/) compares these styles.

Be realistic about noise. A wood fence blocks the view of the road and softens some sound, but it will not make a busy street quiet. Closing the gaps between boards and along the bottom matters as much as adding height. Height also runs into rules, since cities and HOAs often cap how tall a fence can be, so check the limit before you settle on a design.

sections.heading: Setting posts in Goodlettsville rock and clay
paragraphs: Posts are what keep a fence standing, and the ground in Goodlettsville does not always make them easy. Clay soil holds water around the base of a post, which is where wood fence posts usually rot first. Setting the post on a little gravel and crowning the concrete at the top so water runs off helps it last. In some yards, limestone shows up partway down a post hole. A post that hits rock can be drilled in or moved a short distance, but it should not be left short. Every post along the line needs the same depth, so one short post does not become the weak spot.

sections.heading: Fencing a sloped yard in Goodlettsville
paragraphs: Plenty of Goodlettsville backyards slope, some gently and some enough to notice from the back door. On a slope, a fence can be stepped, with each section level and dropping down like stairs. It can also be racked, where the rails follow the angle of the ground. Stepped sections leave triangle gaps at the bottom that a small dog can squeeze through. Racked sections follow the grade more closely but only work with certain styles. If you have a dog, plan how to close those gaps before the fence goes in. The guide on [fencing a sloped yard](/guides/fence-on-a-slope/) has more on picking between the two.

sections.heading: HOA rules and permits for a Goodlettsville fence
paragraphs: In newer Goodlettsville subdivisions, the HOA usually decides which fence styles are allowed and how far forward along the side of the house a fence can go. Many require the finished side to face out toward the neighbors and the street. Send the request with a simple drawing and a photo of the style you want. Then wait for written approval before any posts go in, since pulling out a fence the committee rejects costs real money.

Permits are a separate question. Some offices require one for a fence and some do not, and a pool in the yard can bring extra rules. Pool barriers have their own rules about gates and latches. A Goodlettsville address can fall under more than one codes office depending on the county line, so call the one that covers your lot and ask before you schedule fence installation.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to put up a fence in Goodlettsville?
faqs.a: It depends on where your lot falls. Inside city limits, the City of Goodlettsville codes office says a fence does not need a permit from its building department, but it asks you to call about setback and height rules. On the Davidson side outside the city, Metro Nashville sets the rules, and on the Sumner side the county or a neighboring city may. A short call with your address answers it, and it is worth making before any holes are dug.

faqs.q: Can my new fence go on the same line as the old chain link?
faqs.a: Maybe, but do not assume the old line is right. Chain link on older Goodlettsville lots may have gone up without a survey, and it can sit off the true line in either direction. If the corner pins can be found, measure from them. If not, a survey settles it. Setting the new fence slightly inside your own line is a common way to avoid arguments later.

faqs.q: Will a privacy fence cut the noise from traffic near Rivergate?
faqs.a: Some, but not a lot. A wood privacy fence blocks sight lines well, and that alone can make a yard feel calmer. Sound bends over and around a fence, though, so you will still hear the road. Solid board on board with no gap at the bottom does better than an open style. Shrubs planted on your side add more screening, though they do little for sound.

faqs.q: What happens to tree roots along my fence line?
faqs.a: On established Goodlettsville lots with big shade trees, roots run close to the surface near the trunk. A post hole that hits a small root is fine. A big one is a different story, and cutting it can hurt the tree or even make it less stable. The usual fix is to shift the post a little and adjust the spacing of that section. If a large tree sits right on the line, run the fence a bit off the trunk so the tree has room to grow.

faqs.q: When should I stain a new wood fence?
faqs.a: New pressure treated pine is often still wet from the treatment, and stain does not soak in well until it dries. Many stain makers suggest waiting a while after fence installation. A simple test helps: sprinkle water on a board, and if it soaks in, the wood is ready. Cedar is usually drier and can be stained sooner. In humid Goodlettsville summers, ask about a stain with mildew resistance, especially for sections in shade.
